person: Lan Tran is a 41-year-old pharmacy technician who works rotating shifts and lives with her two children and her mother. Her house was flooded in the valley flood, and she handles all the family's paperwork on her phone. English is her second language, so she reads official letters slowly and sometimes switches her phone to Vietnamese. She has been burned before by a paid helper who did nothing she could not do for free, so she is wary of fees. She has FEMA letters and an insurance settlement letter and is worried she will miss the last day to appeal.
stated_up_front: Hello. FEMA sent me letters about my flood house and some things they did not pay. Can you help me send the appeal before the last day? Please tell me if anything costs money.

facts.about: Date on the FEMA decision letters for house, contents and car
facts.truth: 20 August 2026, so the last day to appeal is Monday 19 October 2026 as the letter shows

facts.about: House repair estimate and what the insurer left unpaid
facts.truth: The repair estimate is 21,300 dollars. The insurer's water-damage limit left 7,300 dollars unpaid. The paper settlement letter in the mail shows this.

facts.about: Contents loss above the insurer's limit
facts.truth: 2,150 dollars above the contents limit was not paid
2,950 dollars of repair, shown by the shop invoice and photos of the car in her photos
The insurer already paid them in full, so she does not want to appeal them
Her brother-in-law's family has a small lake cabin she helped pay for once. It is not her main home and she does not want to appeal for it.
The decision letter is dated 6 August 2026. She missed it and knows the time is over (5 October).
Only a neighbour's estimate of 9,400 dollars for mold. She has no estimate of her own.
A claim service sent an offer for 495 dollars and a contractor asked for a 2,000 dollar deposit. She does not want to pay either.

unknowns: Whether the 60-day appeal rule counts from the letter date or from the day she received the letter
What the insurer's water-damage limit and contents limit are called in the policy, or why they stopped payment
Whether FEMA can pay for things the insurer already paid
What 44 CFR 206.110 to 206.120 say about which items FEMA cannot cover
